analysis.title: Everyone Is Betting On Higher Yields. That's Becoming The Problem.
key_insights: The US 30-year yield printed two consecutive shooting star candles. Yields sit near the upper end of a steep trend channel, well above the 21-day moving average. A pullback is possible without breaking the broader uptrend, and a confirmation candle is needed.
The US 10-year yield is also printing notable candles near the upper end of a steep trend channel, with the 21-day moving average almost 20bps lower.
JPM notes CTA momentum signals in US Treasuries and Bunds reached extreme bearish territory at the end of September. Trend-follower positioning is increasingly vulnerable to mean reversion.

GS CFTC data shows managed money deeply net short US Treasuries, a crowded position. Trend followers were the standout strategy of 2026 (+15.7% over 9M via SG CTA Index), largely on bond shorts and oil longs.
A pause in yields could force CTA shorts to take profits, which would add fuel to a bond bounce.
JPM highlights a divergence: CTAs are heavily short duration while discretionary managers still carry an overhang of long duration exposure. This creates two-way risk.
CTA profit-taking could trigger a tactical bond rally, while further discretionary liquidation could keep yields moving higher.
The Economist ran a cover asking 'Will bonds blow up?' after the bond selloff, which The Market Ear treats as a contrarian signal.
risk_factors: CTA short covering could trigger a tactical bond rally and a drop in yields.
Further discretionary liquidation of long duration could push yields higher.
Crowded short positioning in Treasuries is vulnerable to mean reversion.
